statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 31 U.S.C. § 5324 — Structuring transactions to evade reporting requirements?
statutory.answer: No. 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring to evade reporting requirements, but the facts do not show transactions were structured (e.g., broken into multiple sub-$10,000 cash transactions) or that the business acted with intent to evade CTR reporting.
statutory.label: contradiction
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5324(a) makes it unlawful to (1) cause or attempt to cause a financial institution to fail to file a required report, (2) cause or attempt to cause a financial institution to file a report with a material omission/misstatement, or (3) structure/assist in structuring or attempt to structure a transaction, in each case for the purpose of evading the reporting requirements (e.g., CTRs for currency transactions over $10,000). Here, the cash activity shown includes multiple single cash transactions far above $10,000 (e.g., $103,127.53; $272,691.05; $347,101.88; $175,890.04) and one sub-$10,000 cash deposit ($8,836.66) described as a one-time benign receipt. There is no pattern of breaking a larger cash amount into multiple sub-$10,000 transactions, nor any facts indicating an attempt to cause non-filing or misfiling of CTRs, nor any stated purpose/intent to evade reporting. Therefore, § 5324 prohibits structuring to evade reporting requirements, but the described conduct does not satisfy the statute’s structuring/intent elements.
